newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Italy told EU about IRI capital plan - source.
newsitem.headline: Italy told EU about IRI capital plan - source.

text.p: Italy has informed the European Commission that a capital injection will probably be needed for state-owned industrial holding company IRI, a Commission official told Reuters on Monday.
But the official said he had not yet seen any formal notification of the Italian plans, which the European Union executive would need to examine if state aid was involved.
"It is true that we've been advised by a letter from Mr (Treasury Minister Caro Azeglio) Ciampi that there would be a capital injection before the end of the year probably," the official said.
The Commission had received the letter about a month ago. There was no information about the size of the possible capital injection.
The official was commenting on a report by the Italian news agency ANSA that Italy had asked the EU for permission to grant a capital increase for IRI.

Earlier this month, EU Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert said Italy had asked for a one-year extension of the terms of a 1993 agreement on reducing the industrial holding company's debt, but said he believed only a six-month delay was possible.
The Commission official said the information about the capital increase had been offered at the same time as the request for an extension.
Under the existing accord between Italy and the European Commission, IRI must cut its debt to below 5.0 trillion lire ($3.3 billion) by the end of 1996.

Van Miert said in September he would recommend to the Commission to grant Italy a six-month extension which would be needed because of hitches in Italy's privatisation programme that have delayed the sale of IRI-controlled telecoms holding Stet.
IRI's net debt at the end of 1995 was 22.456 trillion lire. -- Brussels news room, Fredrik Dahl +32 2 287 68 11
